title: Factorising a Negative HCF

findings.finding: The worked examples immediately require numerical and algebraic HCF selection and signed division, but the topic has no opening review of these prior skills.
findings.breakdown: Following the examples requires identifying 8 and 4x as the positive HCFs, then calculating quotients such as 12x÷(−4x)=−3 and −4xy÷(−4x)=y. Weak recall of these skills blocks the new negative-factor procedure.
findings.checked: All supplied teaching was checked. There is no earlier topic or review. p3-information explains the new extraction procedure but assumes students can identify common factors and perform signed algebraic division. These are substantial steps in the examples, rather than incidental calculations or final simplifications.
findings.assumptions: Positive HCF selection and signed algebraic division are prior knowledge. No calculator is assumed; calculator use would not remove the need to identify algebraic factors.

repair.proposal: Before p3-information, add five short review items: (a) Find the positive HCF of 8 and 16. Answer: 8. (b) Find the positive algebraic HCF of 12x and 4xy. Answer: 4x. (c) Calculate −16÷(−8). Answer: 2. (d) Simplify 12x÷(−4x). Answer: −3. (e) Simplify −4xy÷(−4x). Answer: y. Keep the review within one page.

findings.doneWhen: Students rehearse HCF selection and signed division before following the negative-HCF examples.

findings.finding: Extend part a by evaluating its two factorisations at values on either side of the expression’s zero.
findings.breakdown: The follow-up connects equivalent factorisations with the expression’s value and shows how the bracket contributes to its sign.
findings.checked: Part a gives 4(−x+3) and −4(x−3). Both give 4 at x=2 and −4 at x=4; the expression equals zero at x=3. The tasks are concrete follow-ups using the existing expression and require only substitution, signed arithmetic and a simple linear equation.
findings.assumptions: Substitution and solving a simple linear equation are established prior algebra skills in this course.

repair.proposal: Append to p6-q7: (p) Use both factorisations from part a to find the value of −4x+12 when x=2. Answer: 4 from each form. (q) Use both factorisations from part a to find the value of −4x+12 when x=4. Answer: −4 from each form. (r) For what value of x is −4x+12=0? Answer: x=3.

findings.doneWhen: The optional follow-up uses the existing factorisations to compare equal values and locate their shared zero.
